Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important chase! The players are already out in the middle. Hayley Matthews and Qiana Joseph who caused destruction against England will open again for West Indies Women.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, New Zealand Women have a fighting total on the board and they do have the quality in their bowling to defend it. However, looking at how West Indies Women chased in the last game, stopping them is not going to be easy. Both sides will be feeling the pressure, and whoever can keep their nerves better will make it to the final here. Join us in a bit for the exciting second essay.

Suzie Bates is down for a quick chat. She says that there wasn't much of a breeze and the wicket was holding but Georgia Plimmer did well to push through. Mentions that they need to keep taking wickets and the positive thing is that there is something in it for the bowlers. On Chinelle Henry's injury, she says that it is difficult to see and hopes that she recovers soon. Ends by saying that with 130-odd runs on the board, anything can happen.

West Indies Women, on the other hand, looked like they were up for the task from the offset. Despite not getting any wickets in the Powerplay, they kept the runs in check and put pressure on the batters. They dominated the middle overs and kept picking up wickets at regular intervals, but they know they could have done even better. Their catching and fielding were excellent except for one occasion when Chinelle Henry spilled one and got hit on her face. She had to go out and we wish her a speedy recovery. The woman for the big matches, Deandra Dottin was the pick of the bowlers with a four-wicket haul while Afy Fletcher got a couple. Karishma Ramharack and Aaliyah Alleyne also chipped in with one each.

New Zealand Women looked a bit shaky from the start. Maybe it was some nerves of playing in a knockout after a long time. However, they managed to get through the Powerplay scoring 32 runs without losing a wicket. But once Suzie Bates was dismissed, they couldn't really recover from that. There was a period when they started to counterattack through Georgia Plimmer and Sophie Devine, but a break in play cost the former her wicket who was starting to look dangerous scoring 18 off just 9 balls. The Kiwis suffered a collapse after that going from 96/4 to 104/7. It was Izzy Gaze's quick-fire 20 off just 14 balls towards the end that got them over the 125-run mark and with the pitch assisting the spinners, it could be a winning total.

A fantastic bowling performance from West Indies Women! If at the start of the match, they were told that they would restrict the Kiwis under 130, they would have taken it with both hands. However, runs on the board are a crucial thing in a knockout game, and the Kiwi bowlers do have something to play with here.

Just a single to end the first innings! Brilliant bowling from Aaliyah Alleyne as she nails another one right in the blockhole. This is on middle and leg, not much room for the batter either. Izzy Gaze hangs deep and hits it away towards deep mid-wicket for one. They don't push for the second and New Zealand Women finish with 128/9 on the board!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.6: Aaliyah Alleyne to Izzy Gaze, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fran Jonas is the last batter in.

OUT! RUN OUT! Had to be done in order to give Izzy Gaze a fighting chance on the final delivery. Aaliyah Alleyne goes full again and nails it right around the front boot. Eden Carson manages to dig it out but gets it right back at the bowler. Grace is already halfway down the pitch and Carson starts running as well. Alleyne jogs back and whips off the bails to send Carson back to the hut.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.5: Aaliyah Alleyne to Eden Carson, OUT! run out (Aaliyah Alleyne).

Commentary.Commentary: Eden Carson comes out to the middle now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Heart in the mouth moment for Qiana Joseph there but she manages to hang on to the ball. Aaliyah Alleyne continues from around the stumps and darts across a full ball on middle, angling it away. Lea Tahuhu hangs back and tries to make room in order to open up the off side but ends up slicing it up around the cover region. Joseph moves to her right and pouches the ball but it pops out and she holds onto it on the second attempt.

Commentary.Commentary: Just over the infield! Pitched up outside off, Grace steps out and lifts the ball over Karishma Ramharack at covers and picks up a couple of runs.

This one dips late and nips in, beating the attempted defense of Rosemary Mair. The ball goes past the inside edge and hits the pads. West Indies Women do review it and there's nothing on UltraEdge. Ball Tracking though comes up with three reds and the decision is overturned. Excellent review and Dottin has four wickets!

Commentary.Commentary: Rosemary Mair walks out to bat now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Deandra Dottin is rolling back the years and is putting on a stellar show in a big match yet again for West Indies Women. Lovely deception from Dottin as she bowls the leg cutter, on a hard length over off and middle. This one holds a bit in the deck and just nibbles away. Maddy Green gets caught on the crease looking to work it away but gets a leading edge that pops up high and just to the silly point region. The keeper, Shemaine Campbelle calls for it and runs in to take the catch. New Zealand Women losing the plot here.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle, Sophie Devine flicks it through square leg for one. End of another successful over from Deandra Dottin!

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on off, Maddy Green drives it through covers for one.

OUT! CASTLED! And it happens again! Another halt in play and New Zealand Women lose a wicket. Deandra Dottin steams in and serves another excellent yorker, on middle and off. Brooke Halliday may be still thinking about the last ball, fails to get her bat down in time and the ball rattles the off pole. A quick cameo of 18 off 9 from Halliday comes to an end now!

Commentary.Commentary: Another slight halt in play as that last throw seems to have hit Brooke Halliday flush on the left boot or near the ankle and that is a painful blow to take. Halliday seems to be fine but the physio does come out to have a look and probably apply some magic spray. A couple of minutes later, we are good to go again.

Fuller and on the pads, Brooke Halliday clips it away through mid-wicket for another two. The fielder throws it at the keeper's end where the ball hits the ankle of Halliday as she falls over after crossing the crease.

Commentary.Commentary: Well bowled! Deandra Dottin nails the yorker, just outside off, Brooke Halliday backs away and only manages to dig it out on the pitch.

Commentary.Commentary: Overpitched and outside off, Sophie Devine drills it wide of long off for just a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Right in the blockhole, on leg, Brooke Halliday tucks it with soft hands towards the square leg region and comes back for the second run. Excellent running. 12 runs off the over. 24 in the last two!

Commentary.Commentary: Touch fuller but down the leg side, Sophie Devine fails to flick it away. It is called a wide. Oh..wait! That call needs to be changed as Alleyne has overstepped here. No Ball! Free Hit up next...
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 13.5: Aaliyah Alleyne to Sophie Devine, No ball!

Commentary.Commentary: Slower one, on a length and on off, Sophie Devine steers it towards point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 13.4: Aaliyah Alleyne to Sophie Devine, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! No stopping that one! Aaliyah Alleyne goes a bit too full and around off, Sophie Devine gets underneath it and creams it through covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 13.3: Aaliyah Alleyne to Sophie Devine, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and on middle, Sophie Devine pulls it towards deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 13.1: Aaliyah Alleyne to Sophie Devine, 1 run.

Stafanie Taylor runs to her right and tries to stop it with her foot in the end but lets it through for a boundary. 12 runs off the over but a wicket too!

Commentary.Commentary: Shortish and on middle, Brooke Halliday swipes it to deep mid-wicket for a brace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 12.5: Afy Fletcher to Brooke Halliday, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Much-needed boundary for the Kiwis! Tossed up, full and on middle, Brooke Halliday skips down the track to get to the pitch of it and heaves it towards the deep mid-wicket fence for four runs.

OUT! STUMPED! 9th wicket for Afy Fletcher in this World Cup! She sees the batter come down the track and bowls this very slower through the air, keeps it away from the batter as well, on off. Georgia Plimmer is halfway down the track for the big slog but gets beaten by the flight and Shemaine Campbelle behind the stumps does the rest. Plimmer goes back after a well-made 33 off 31, and she is now the leading run-scorer in this tournament. Another timely wicket for West Indies Women!
Commentary.Howout: st Shemaine Campbelle b Afy Fletcher
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 12.1: Afy Fletcher to Georgia Plimmer, OUT! st Shemaine Campbelle b Afy Fletcher.

Commentary.Commentary: A full toss, on middle, Sophie Devine flicks it away wide of deep mid-wicket for a brace. 6 runs and a wicket from an eventful first over from Deandra Dottin!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 11.6: Deandra Dottin to Sophie Devine, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up and on off, Sophie Devine drills it towards mid off for a quick single.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length and around off, Sophie Devine stabs it to the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 11.3: Deandra Dottin to Sophie Devine, No run.

This is full and just outside off, Melie Kerr comes down the track to clear the infield. However, she has to reach for it a bit and ends up mistiming it straight to mid off where Karishma Ramharack makes no mistake. New Zealand Women two down now!

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, dear! That ball has gone straight through the hands and into the face of Chinelle Henry, she seemed to have lost it in the light. The replays show that the ball hit Henry's forehead and the physio is out to have a look. Hopefully, she is fine. A concussion test is being performed but the good news is that she is up on her feet and is walking back to the dressing room with the medical team.

DROPPED! And that is a NASTY BLOW for Chinelle Henry! Deandra Dottin starts with a back-of-a-length delivery, on off. Melie Kerr pulls it but does not get the connection right as the ball flies towards deep mid-wicket. Henry runs forward and tries to reverse cup it, but the ball goes through and hits her flush on the forehead. She is down in a lot of pain and there are a lot of concerned faces around the ground.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 11.1: Deandra Dottin to Melie Kerr, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Slows it up, full and around off, Melie Kerr steps across and clips it through square leg for one.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 10.5: Karishma Ramharack to Georgia Plimmer, 1 run.

Chinelle Henry comes forward a bit too much and then tries to leap up to grab it with her outstretched left hand. But the ball goes over her for a biggie. If she was close to the ropes, it would have been an easy catch.

It looked like the impact is outside off, but the Windies take the review here. UltraEdge confirms no bat involved. Ball Tracking shows exactly what we suspected. West Indies Women lose a review!

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, short and on middle, Melie Kerr uses her feet and pats it down to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 10.1: Karishma Ramharack to Melie Kerr, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! Despite not scoring a lot, the good thing for the Kiwis is that they have lost only one wicket. They have a good platform from where one batter can anchor the innings and the others play the attacking role. West Indies Women have bowled and fielded well, but will like to pick up a few wickets because as we know teams with wickets in hand tend to score a lot in the death overs. An exciting phase of cricket awaits us.
A dot to end and New Zealand Women are 54/1 at the halfway mark! Aaliyah Alleyne persists with the fuller length and nails it into the blockhole around middle, Plimmer can only manage to dig it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 9.6: Aaliyah Alleyne to Georgia Plimmer, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Georgia Plimmer playing with fire there! Pre-meditates for the lap and Aaliyah Alleyne bowls it right around the top of middle and leg. Plimmer misses on the connection and the ball goes just over the stumps.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to get the repeat of the 2016 semi-final underway! The umpires are out in the middle and the players of West Indies Women can be seen in a huddle after which they pump themselves up and walk onto the field of play. The duo of veteran Suzie Bates and Georgia Plimmer is all set to open the innings for New Zealand Women. Chinelle Henry has the new ball in hand and is ready to steam in. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from this engrossing clash. The stage is set, the crowd is in and the players are out along with their mascots, lining up for the national anthems of the two teams. The officials and the coveted trophy is what is stands between the teams and first up, it is the national anthem of New Zealand followed by the national anthem of West Indies.

PITCH REPORT - Lydia Greenway is inspecting the deck. She says that there is a nice breeze and the temperatures are a bit cooler from the start of the tournament. Informs that pitch 5 is being used which was used on the first day of the tournament. Anjum Chopra joins her and says that there is a nice green cover and the pitch is well rested as well.

Hayley Matthews, the captain of West Indies Women says that they wanted to bowl anyway as they have done well chasing in this tournament. Adds that everyone in the dressing room is hungry and wants to take the last two steps. Mentions that it is good to see the teams from the middle of the groups making it here which shows that the world game is growing. Informs Stafanie Taylor is back in the side and Chedean Nation misses out.

Sophie Devine, the skipper of New Zealand Women want runs on the board. Adds that the schedule has been kind for them and they have been able to train and implement a few different things that might be useful in this game. Informs that it is the same team and are looking forward to start from scratch.

West Indies Women (Playing XI) - Hayley Matthews (C), Qiana Joseph, Shemaine Campbelle (WK), Deandra Dottin, Stafanie Taylor (In place of Chedean Nation), Chinelle Henry, Aaliyah Alleyne, Zaida James, Afy Fletcher, Ashmini Munisar, Karishma Ramharack.

New Zealand Women (Unchanged Playing XI) - Suzie Bates, Georgia Plimmer, Melie Kerr, Sophie Devine (C), Brooke Halliday, Maddy Green, Izzy Gaze (WK), Rosemary Mair, Lea Tahuhu, Eden Carson, Fran Jonas.
TOSS - Hayley Matthews flips the coin and Sophie Devine correctly calls 'Heads'. New Zealand Women have elected to BAT first.

As the coin flip approaches, the tension and excitement are building rapidly. With two top-quality teams eager to fight for a place in the final, we're in for a thrilling showdown. If the West Indies Women make it through, they could become the only team besides Australia to win the title twice. On the other hand, if New Zealand Women secures a spot, we’re guaranteed a new champion. So, who are you backing? Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

West Indies Women had to battle hard through the group stages. After a heavy opening defeat to South Africa, they bounced back with three consecutive wins. Their standout moment came when they ended a 13-match losing streak against England in a virtual knockout. This victory was extra special as it marked Hayley Matthews' 100th T20I, and she led her side back to where they belonged. The return of Deandra Dottin has been crucial, as she thrives in high-pressure moments with both bat and ball. Although their middle order has been inconsistent, Qiana Joseph did impress with a match-winning knock after getting promoted in the last game. However, the bowling has been good with Karishma Ramharack and Afy Fletcher expertly exploiting the spin-friendly conditions. A key factor for them has been their six-hitting ability, smashing 12 sixes in the group stages - far outstripping others as no one even hit 5, making them dangerous in the low-scoring conditions of the UAE.

The White Ferns kicked off their campaign in style, dominating India in a convincing win. Despite a setback against Australia, they bounced back impressively, winning their next two matches to secure a semi-final spot. Sophie Devine’s leadership has been outstanding, and both her and Suzie Bates' vast experience will be crucial in this high-stakes match. Melie Kerr’s all-round brilliance has added great balance, while Rosemary Mair and Eden Carson have excelled in leading the pace and spin attacks respectively. Coming into the tournament with a poor run of form, New Zealand now finds themselves just two wins away from potentially becoming the first New Zealand team, across any format and gender, to lift a World Cup.

West Indies Women return to the semi-finals for the first time since 2018, and guess who they knocked out on their title-winning run back in 2016? That’s right, New Zealand Women. However, back in 2010, it was the Kiwis who emerged victorious against the Windies in the semis. But this time around, the stakes are different, and no one saw these two sides making it this far. Yet, cricket is a game full of surprises. The heavyweights - Australia, India, and England have all been knocked out. New Zealand, runners-up in the inaugural edition in 2009, have impressed in the group stages, and they’ll be confident of reaching their first final in 15 long years.

And then there were three! In an unforgettable moment last night, South Africa Women shattered Australia's dominance to secure their spot in a second consecutive T20 World Cup final. Now, the burning question remains - who will step up to face them in the ultimate showdown? Will the epitome of 'So close, yet so far', New Zealand Women finally seize their moment of glory, or will the 2016 champions, West Indies Women, reclaim their place at the top? Only time will reveal the answer. A warm welcome to all as we gear up for the 2nd Semi-Final of the 2024 Women's T20 World Cup at the iconic Sharjah Cricket Stadium!
... MATCH DAY ...

The stage is set as the top four teams in the ICC Women's T20 World Cup, 2024 battle it out for eternal glory in the semi-final stage of the competition. In the second semi-final, the table toppers from Group B, West Indies Women will take on Group A's runners-up, New Zealand Women in Sharjah as both sides look to secure a passage in the Final. West Indies Women journey to the semi-final has been nothing sort of a miracle as they pulled off a thunderous victory against the inaugural Women's T20 World Cup winners, England Women in their final group game, sending their opponents packing out of the tournament as well. New Zealand Women on the other hand defeated India Women in their first clash and then a couple of other Asian power houses, losing only to their Trans-Tasmanian rivals Australia Women in the process. Talking more about the teams, it was not an ideal start for West Indies Women as they were hammered by South Africa who won that match by 10 wickets. However, the women from the Caribbean recovered quickly and notched up a couple comprehensive wins against the likes of Scotland and Bangladesh to get that net run rate in the positive and when the do-or-die game came against England, skipper Hayley Matthews led from the front and with the support of Qiana Joseph and Deandra Dottin with the bat, chased down 140-plus runs with a couple of overs to go. New Zealand Women on the other hand came into the T20 World Cup having lost 10 T20 matches in a row but a monumental performance against India in their first game saw the tables turn. They did get bundled out for just 88 runs against the Aussies but put on a couple of commanding performances with the ball against Sri Lanka and especially Pakistan to make their way into the knockout stage of the competition. The likes of Sophie Devine and Melie Kerr will be key for the success of White Ferns and overall it should be an engrossing watch as two teams from opposite parts of the globe look to keep their dream alive of lifting the coveted trophy. Who are you backing for the win?
